_comment: An entry belongs here only when a Python-emitting template ('*.py.j2') is
CORRECT to carry a doubled backslash before n/t/r -- for example a template
emitting Python that in turn writes a shell script needing a literal escape.
Each entry pins the file AND the exact matched line, so it cannot widen into
a whole-file allowance as the template changes around it. An entry whose line
no longer exists fails the gate rather than lingering.
expected_count must equal the number of entries: remediation removes the entry
and decrements the count in the same change.

exemptions.snippet: several metadata/units lines before the header. ``csv|delimiter=\\t`` selects a
exemptions.reason: Documentation of a user-authored format hint, not a string the program builds. The emitted _parse_csv_spec decodes the hint with value.encode().decode('unicode_escape'), so the caller writes the two literal characters backslash-t; the docstring must therefore render them literally, which a non-raw docstring does only when doubled. A single backslash here would put a real tab character in the docstring and misdocument the API.

exemptions.snippet: single-character delimiter other than comma (e.g. ``\\t`` for TSV).
exemptions.reason: Same format-hint documentation on _parse_csv, the function that consumes the decoded delimiter. See the _json_parse_tabular entry above.
